comparator.name: Bachelor Computer Science and Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The official February 2026 curriculum chart and current programme page define a three-year, 180-EC programme. Year 1 contains twelve compulsory 5-EC courses (60 EC). Year 2 contains six compulsory 5-EC core courses, Computer Security (5 EC), two 5-EC electives and a 15-EC Software Project (60 EC). Year 3 contains a 30-EC minor, three 5-EC electives and a 15-EC Research Project (60 EC). For the five elective slots, the reconstruction selects the five named current example topics advertised by TU Delft: Computer Graphics, Big Data Processing, Deep Learning, Bioinformatics and Software Engineering with AI.

alternatives.label: Software, systems and algorithms
alternatives.concept: Builds a computer-science pathway around programming, software development, databases, networks and operating systems, algorithms, discrete mathematics, probability and selected AI methods. It is the closest feasible UCR response to TU Delft CSE, while not reproducing TU Delft’s computer-organisation, formal-languages, programming-languages, security and large compulsory project sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum sustains programming, software, computer systems, algorithms and mathematical foundations across all three years.
progression: Programming, data and mathematical foundations precede databases, systems, software development, advanced algorithms and AI. Every prerequisite and planned 2026–29 term offering was checked in the current enriched workbook.

alternatives.label: AI, data and computational modelling
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, algorithms and responsible computing while shifting the advanced programme toward linear algebra, numerical and systems modelling, probability, optimisation, machine learning and neural networks. It develops TU Delft CSE’s explicit AI, data and computational-modelling interests as a coherent second direction.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines a computing core with sustained mathematical modelling, statistics, optimisation and machine learning.
progression: Programming, database, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced algorithms, probability, optimisation, machine learning and neural networks. Every prerequisite and planned 2026–29 term offering was checked in the current enriched workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, Research Methods & Statistics, business foundations, digital transformation, market research, linear systems, sociology and experimental methods replace product design, philosophy, networks and operating systems, software development, advanced algorithms, computer vision, reinforcement learning and AI decision-making. The 67.5-EC shift follows the evidenced AI/data/modelling emphasis and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC floor.

blocks: Introduction to Programming directly addresses programming fundamentals, with different language and project scope.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics directly addresses formal reasoning and discrete structures.
Software Development addresses software design and implementation, but not TU Delft’s complete engineering sequence.
Algorithms & Data Structures directly addresses algorithmic design and data structures.
Advanced Algorithms develops algorithm analysis and design beyond the introductory UCR course.
UCR has relevant logic and algorithms, but no selected course reproduces formal languages, computability and complexity as one dedicated course.
UCR has programming and software development, but no selected course dedicated to programming-language concepts.
Computer systems, data management and security
UCR has no selected course dedicated to computer architecture and organisation.
Database Management Systems directly addresses database modelling, storage and querying.
Networks & Operating Systems directly addresses network design and operation, with broader combined scope.
Networks & Operating Systems is already aligned to Computer Networks and is not duplicated; TU Delft has a separate operating-systems course.
AI Ethics addresses responsible computing but does not reproduce TU Delft’s technical computer-security course.
Mathematical Methods develops calculus-based methods used for computational modelling, with different breadth.
Linear Algebra directly addresses vectors, matrices and computational linear methods.
Research Methods & Statistics addresses statistical inference and empirical design, with less probability theory.
Introduction to Data Science addresses data handling, analysis and visualisation, at a broader introductory level.
Decision-making in AI develops one substantive area of artificial intelligence, without reproducing the full survey course.
Machine Learning directly addresses supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
Image Processing & Computer Vision addresses computational image and visual methods within the advertised graphics elective space.
Neural Networks & Deep Learning directly addresses the advertised deep-learning elective topic.
UCR has no selected course dedicated to bioinformatics.
UCR software and AI courses appear elsewhere; no course is duplicated against this combined elective.
Human-centred design, communication and responsible technology
Consumer Product Design uses user research, prototyping and evaluation, but does not reproduce the full HCI and AI-assisted prototyping course.
Academic formation, engineering projects and research
UCR has collaborative coursework, but no selected 5-EC course dedicated to a software development project.
UCR has no 15-EC compulsory external-client software project.
TU Delft reserves 30 EC for a broadening minor or study abroad. UCR’s entire curriculum is already an interdisciplinary liberal-arts-and-sciences programme.
TU Delft requires a 15-EC individual computer-science research project; UCR optional independent research is shown separately by the compiler.

candidates.label: Human-centred computing, graphics and digital society

selection.assessment: The closest programme is a defensible 24-course response to TU Delft’s programming, software, algorithms, systems, mathematics, data and AI core. A second coherent curriculum follows the explicit AI, data and computational-modelling cluster and passes all feasibility and pairwise-distinctness rules. A third human-centred graphics direction was tested, but the current UCR inventory does not contain enough distinct HCI, computer-graphics and software-systems courses to sustain a third 24-course computing programme without padding it with merely adjacent social-science or business courses.

notes.text: TU Delft CSE includes dedicated computer organisation, theoretical computer science, programming languages, computer security, a compulsory collaborative-development project, a 15-EC external-client software project and a 15-EC individual research project. UCR offers substantial programming, databases, systems, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but neither alternative reproduces that complete engineering sequence. TU Delft also reserves 30 EC for a minor and 25 EC for CSE electives.
